pageCache.text:
Well-being, Pastoral Care and SEND
Because We Care
The well-being of our pupils is at the heart of everything we do at Shoreham College. We firmly believe that a happy, well-cared for child who feels safe and secure will flourish academically and socially.
As a community, we work hard to enhance well-being; nurturing each individual child and developing meaningful relationships with them.
Safeguarding is the most important thing we do at Shoreham College. It comes first, and it takes precedence. Nothing matters more. Our Designated Safeguarding Lead and two deputy Designated Safeguarding Leads work closely with staff to ensure that pupils are safe in school and safe as they go about their lives. We believe in early intervention, and we work carefully with families and the children themselves to provide help and support, and to keep our pupils safe.
We all have physical and mental health. We want you to know that there are very few things that your child is experiencing, or that you are experiencing as a family, that we have not seen before. We will work with you to help you. Every situation, every child, and every family is unique, and if we cannot help, please know that we will listen and support, and that we are experienced in signposting you to other sources of support and expertise. Prevention is better than cure and so we aim to identify and deal with any issues as they occur, and when they are still small.
Excellent pastoral care is at the centre of our education. All of our pupils have a form teacher, who is the first port of call for assistance with any concern, enquiry, or request. In the Senior School, tutors remain with their form group from Year 7 to Year 11. This continuity ensures that the relationship between the tutor and tutee is meaningful and supportive, and that each child, and their family, is known and valued. Our assistant heads support our caring pastoral teams.
We understand that it is sometimes important to talk to a professional about concerns and worries. A Dialogue YMCA counsellor is on hand to assist pupils with any issues they may face, and children can self-refer to this service. We work closely with Allsorts, our local LGBTQ+ advisors, and the Diana Award, a charity committed to developing anti-bullying strategies. At any time, we have a strong team ready to help. The team, which includes our Designated Safeguarding Lead and deputy Designated Safeguarding Leads, is always available.
Our caring matron assists pupils with minor ailments or illness, and we have a team of trained mental health first aiders for when children need emotional support or even some good ol’ TLC.
Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND)
As an inclusive school, which is broadly non-selective, Shoreham College has excellent SEND provision. Our qualified and experienced SENCO ensures that pupils with SEND needs receive all the appropriate support.
We are a mainstream school, and if we do not have the specialist facilities to cater for your child’s needs, we endeavour to support you in your search for a school better equipped to support your child.
We will work with parents to make adjustments where we can do so, but always with appropriate regard to the needs of other students and the resources available to the school.
All pupils belong to one of four houses: Grenville, Nelson, Rodney, and Raleigh, named in recognition of our local maritime heritage. Pupils remain with their house throughout their school career. Fostering a team spirit and a sense of belonging, our houses add fun, flavour, and healthy competition to our community, and each week pupils from Year 5 to Year 11 assemble with staff members to prepare for a forthcoming occasion or event. Our calendar of house events and competitions is a busy one. Members of each house join forces to compete in public speaking, the arts, poetry recitals, drama, and our spirited House Music competition. House competitions for sport include netball, football, rugby, and cricket as well as a popular swimming gala. There is fiercely friendly rivalry, but the focus of all events is always on enjoyment, teamwork, inclusion, and personal development. A varied house programme ensures that all children are enthused and involved.
Our house system offers plenty of opportunities for rewarding positive behaviour. Pupils win points for their houses through academic work or positive behaviour that benefits others. Our houses collaborate to raise money for local charities, and a favourite fundraiser is the Winter Fayre, a festive and lively occasion, where each house runs a stall.
The Head of House plays an important role in involving the pupils in a variety of house activities, and each year, every house elects two Year 11 pupils to the prestigious role of House Captain. Positive role models, House Captains help to run the weekly house meetings, promote the success of their house, and support their fellow members in effective collaboration and participation.
Our peer mentoring scheme makes a very positive contribution to pastoral care. Pupils in Year 10 and 11 can volunteer to be peer mentors for younger pupils, meeting their counterparts fortnightly in interactions supported by a member of staff. The peer mentor lends a listening ear, offers friendship and academic advice, and acts like an older sibling in school – looking out for their younger buddy in a way that enriches both their mentee’s experience and their own. These gentle connections are powerful for well-being.
SCHOOL COUNCIL AND PUPIL VOICE
Shoreham College children know their school. They understand what is working well, what they enjoy, and what they would like to improve. Pupils want their school to succeed. When the adults around them listen carefully, our children’s experiences have a profound impact on the success of the school. At Shoreham College, we prioritise open, effective communication between our children and our staff. Our School Council offers a formal forum for pupils to make their voices heard and to offer suggestions and comments. Whether we are discussing GCSE options, catering, co-curricular activities, or uniform, it is important that pupils have a formal route to communicate their ideas and become involved in the discussion. Most importantly, School Council is a forum where the staff listens to children’s views on school issues.
Pupil voice is rich in that it enables adults to understand children’s experience of school and to improve that experience to better suit their needs. When people feel heard, they know they are valued. Demonstrating to children that their voice is important and can advocate for positive change helps to improve their confidence, self-esteem, and well-being. Our children learn that we listen and that we consider and discuss a variety of factors with them before coming to a decision. In many instances, we are delighted to give a resounding yes to our children’s proposals, but not always. We prepare our young people well when we help them to fight for the yes and have the resilience to accept a well-considered no.
Mindfulness can improve our physical and mental health, help our focus and engagement, and enhance our ability to live in the moment. Shoreham College is a beacon school for mindfulness. We recognise it plays a key role in well-being and have developed mindfulness programmes for pupils of all ages. Our programmes run as part of the PSHE curriculum and within our co-curricular provision.
SPORT AND THE OUTDOORS
At Shoreham College, we understand that sport is about more than competition. It develops our minds and bodies, boosting our immune systems and developing key skills. Our holistic programme encourages participation and healthy enjoyment. Teamwork and resilience in the face of tough opposition develop our young people’s ability to overcome obstacles and find strength in others. Learning how to win, and lose and bounce back, helps them to see themselves as part of a larger picture and to develop a growth mindset.
Fresh air is good for the mind, body, and soul, and our whole school has access to lots of it within our 11-acre site’s extensive playing fields and woodland. At Shoreham College, our appreciation of the great outdoors and nature starts young. Our Little Lions love their designated outdoor learning areas, outside spaces, and woodland experiences. Our junior and senior pupils also enjoy many opportunities to access the natural world and benefit from our thriving forest school. Working with the local South Downs National Park and the John Muir Award encourages junior pupils to connect with, enjoy, and care for wild places whilst developing key skills. Our senior pupils range over the South Downs National Park as part of the Duke of Edinburgh Award Scheme, and enjoy mountain adventure training in Snowdonia. Shoreham College prioritises time to engage the inner animal and remember what it is like to smell the wind, listen to the trees, and get your hands dirty!
Freshly cooked food, with locally sourced ingredients, graces our Shoreham College tables daily, thanks to the dedication of the inventive chefs in our on-site kitchen.
Using only the best ingredients from local farmers and artisan suppliers, we strive to wow our pupils, whilst keeping the traditional touches. Excellent nutrition is imperative to children’s healthy growth and mindset, and our chefs prepare our food using methods that preserve its natural goodness and high nutritional value.
Each lunchtime, we offer a vast array of food choices to appeal to every child’s tastes. These include two hot main dishes (one of which is vegetarian), pasta, jacket potatoes, soup, wraps, cold meats, and an expansive salad bar. For dessert, our talented pastry chef always prepares something tempting, and there is a choice of fresh fruits and yoghurt.

Senior Curriculum
Senior Curriculum
At Shoreham College, we believe that every child is important, unique and talented, and deserves an enriched and rounded education. Our broadly non-selective policy enables us to fulfil our commitment to providing an education to children of varied ability so that they can achieve their potential. Our children follow a broad curriculum, which is challenging and supportive in equal measure and shows them that, with hard work, they are able to achieve almost anything.
Ambitious for our children, we believe a true education includes and extends beyond excellent achievement. Committed to enabling every child to attain their academic potential, we strive to develop the skills and qualities they will need for confident success in their studies and lives. A beacon school for mindfulness, we instil in our pupils compassionate self-care and consideration of others. Happy children are successful children, and we foster a friendly, caring community with our children’s well-being at its heart.
Thinking skills and independent learning are cultivated through a broad variety of subjects, following the national curriculum. Our pupils develop resilience and confidence through experiencing success in a range of areas and through following their passions. We assist pupils in making the most of their abilities and in choosing a wide and balanced GCSE curriculum for which they are well prepared and supported. An exhilarating co-curricular programme, including forest school, charitable endeavours, and the Youth Parliament Democracy Awards, enhances our academic provision, allowing our children to expand their skills and experiences.
Our children play an active role in their learning, and we work closely with parents and pupils to set clear targets and ensure excellent academic progress. The Challenge Grade Reporting System informs parents of their child’s progress each half-term.
Effective preparation and the long-term cultivation of skills necessary for success help pupils to excel in public examinations. As the public examinations approach, we provide targeted revision sessions, workshops on examination technique, and comprehensive support for pupils’ well-being. Our sixth form exhibition and careers sessions educate pupils about their post GCSE choices, enabling them to make informed decisions and head confidently into their future lives.

Co-curricular
Senior Co-curricular
Shoreham College is committed to educating the whole person, and our co-curricular programme is central to our provision.
By the time our young people leave us, we hope that they have enjoyed a wide range of experiences and challenges that will help shape them and prepare them for the future. Sports enable our pupils to develop self-discipline, a sense of fairness, and commitment, and as our Duke of Edinburgh Award Scheme participants will attest, there is nothing better to develop your sense of humour and resilience than being lost on a windy Sussex Down in the rain with your map upside down: a great challenge!
During their time at Shoreham College, from age 3 until they leave us in Year 11, we introduce our children to a wide variety of experiences through sport, music, drama, our Leadership and Skills initiative, and our activities programme, which runs every evening from 4pm to 5pm.
We vary our after school activities each year to respond to our pupils’ interests. Over the years, pupils have enjoyed Kung Fu, textiles, art, astronomy club, chess club, LAMDA, and cookery. We continue to expand our programme to include outdoor education, woodland, and wildlife.
At Shoreham College, we encourage our pupils to challenge themselves, try new things, and thereby discover aspects of their personalities and qualities that they perhaps did not even know existed. There are terrific educational benefits to be had too, and pupils develop their knowledge and understanding and a diverse range of skills.
Our co-curricular programme allows every pupil at Shoreham College to participate, learn, develop, and have fun. As our school motto states, ‘God gives us the hour’, and we certainly make the most of it!

Careers
Welcome to our Careers Page
At Shoreham College, we encourage every young person to think ambitiously about their future.
From the earliest years through to senior school, pupils are supported to develop curiosity, confidence, and a growing sense of possibility about the pathways open to them.
Pupils begin exploring the world beyond the classroom from a young age. In the Early Years, this may involve meeting members of the local community, such as firefighters, while pupils in Years 5 and 6 are introduced to a range of STEM-related careers. These early experiences are designed to broaden understanding and spark interest, rather than narrow choices.
As pupils move into the senior school, careers education becomes more structured. In Year 7, pupils take part in a dedicated week of Careers Breakfasts, meeting external speakers who share their experiences and routes into work. In Year 8, pupils attend our ‘Get Inspired’ event, designed to broaden horizons at a point when many young people begin to limit their aspirations too early.
In Years 9 and 10, pupils take part in increasingly practical careers experiences. Year 9 pupils attend The BIG Futures Show, East Sussex’s largest employability, skills, and careers event, engaging directly with employers, training providers, and industry professionals. In Year 10, pupils follow a focused two-day programme that includes talks from professionals across a range of sectors, CV development, and mock interviews with personalised feedback.
Alongside these events, pupils benefit from STEM days, university experience visits, and a structured PSHE and Morrisby programme. Together, our careers provision supports pupils to make informed choices, build self-belief, and move forward with confidence into the next stage of their education and beyond.

Scholarships
Scholarships
Shoreham College offers a range of scholarships.
In Year 6, the Assistant Principal (Juniors), and their team nominate the pupils who will be eligible to apply for a scholarship. These pupils may then begin the application process.
External applicants for any of our scholarships should take advice from their current head teacher, who should endorse any application in writing by way of a formal reference. Please email applications and references to [email protected], or submit them by post to the Principal of Shoreham College, Shoreham College, St Julian’s Lane, Shoreham by Sea, West Sussex, BN43 6YW.
The following scholarships are available every year for Year 6 pupils:
Guidance
Art scholars tend to be those who are recognised as exceptional performers or artists (or both). They are children who truly excel as dramatists, singers, performers, painters, or musicians. Their work across more than one area is outstanding.
Sport scholars are usually young people who are exceptional in several sports and play at a high level of club sport, or in county squads, and often hold captaincies and similar positions.
Academic scholars are children performing in the top 10% of a year group. They are likely to have been recognised early on in their school careers as someone who might go on to study A-levels and potentially attend a Russell Group university.
All-rounders are those who are genuinely good at a wide range of disciplines and who show real leadership potential. They may have held positions of responsibility in their current schools, such as form captain or prefect.
How to Apply
All candidates who have been officially selected receive an application pack which explains the scholarship processes.
The deadline for receipt of the full scholarship application form and supporting evidence, for all types of scholarship, varies from year to year (normally falling in the Lent term). Please contact the school for details.
The results and interviews are considered by the Principal, working in conjunction with the General Manager (Clerk to the Governors) and the Chair of the Finance and General Purposes Committee. Parents will be notified of the outcome of the candidates’ applications within two weeks of the close of the application process.
For further details, please refer to our Registrar, Mrs Hall, who can be contacted on 01273 592681 or [email protected].

School Transport
School Transport
Shoreham College runs a fleet of minibuses for children from Year 5 upwards. We span the area from Brighton in the east to Littlehampton in the west, and Storrington and Hurstpierpoint in the north.
The service operates Monday to Friday term time only, and there is a small charge per term. Please see our fees page for more details.
Collection is from 7.30am, and the services depart from school at 5.00pm.
Exact times, locations, and routes vary according to demand.
Should you wish to use any of the minibus services, please contact Shoreham College for availability and costs. Places are offered on a first-come, first-served basis.
Please note that all our minibuses are maintained under current legislation, and all drivers are fully qualified and DBS checked.

Junior Curriculum
Junior Curriculum
At Shoreham College, we believe that every child is important, unique, and talented, and deserves an enriched and rounded education. Our largely non-selective policy enables us to fulfil our commitment to providing an education to children of varied ability so that they can achieve their potential. Our children follow a broad curriculum, which is challenging and supportive in equal measure and shows them that, with hard work, they are able to achieve almost anything.
Our excellent academic education mainly follows the national curriculum and current literacy and numeracy frameworks. We place great emphasis on strong foundation skills in numeracy, including problem-solving and mental arithmetic and their application in the wider world, and in literacy where pupils follow a structured phonics programme. Cared for principally by their class teacher, children enjoy specialist teaching in French and Spanish, Design Technology, Music, and Physical Education. Our expansive curriculum includes Art, Religious Studies, Drama, and Food Technology, offering much to engage and inspire our pupils. Small teaching groups and differentiated work provide perfect balance between support and challenge, ensuring every child reaches their potential. Our teachers work closely with each child and their families to provide a tailored, motivating, and positive learning experience. We are always available to discuss pupil progress and development.
We adopt a creative approach to enhance and deepen our pupils’ knowledge and understanding of our vibrant curriculum. Combining literature with a thematic approach, Junior Challenges allow children to explore, discover, and challenge themselves whilst making connections and developing higher level thinking. From ‘Our Amazing World’ and Michael Morpurgo’s Kensuke’s Kingdom in Year 6 to Vikings, invaders, and dragon training in Year 3, we offer abundant awe and wonder.
We seek to extend our children’s personal skills and experiences, supporting them to work collaboratively and respect different viewpoints. Forest school and mindfulness encourage pupils to become resilient and reflective learners. A stimulating co-curricular programme, including the John Muir Award Scheme, enriches our children’s learning and provides opportunities for them to develop as compassionate, confident individuals.
Our all-through, fully integrated school allows our junior pupils to interact with children of all ages, learning from older children and developing leadership qualities as role models to younger pupils. As our pupils are already known and valued members of our community, the transition to our Senior School is smooth, and their strong progress is maintained.

Pre-School Curriculum
Little Lions Curriculum
At Shoreham College, we believe that every child is important, unique, and talented, and deserves an enriched and rounded education. Our broadly non-selective policy enables us to fulfil our commitment to providing an education to children of varied ability so that they can achieve their potential. Our children follow a broad curriculum, which is challenging and supportive in equal measure and shows them that, with hard work, they are able to achieve almost anything.
Our Little Lions’ curriculum offers an inspirational learning journey. Passionate in supporting all children to achieve their full, unique potential, we value every child and foster mutual respect and a calm, caring environment.
In line with the EYFS framework, we encourage a positive attitude to school and learning, setting high expectations and helping our children to be kind, work hard, and never give up. These foundations are embedded in all aspects of our children’s lives as they become lifelong learners within our wider school community.
Our younger pupils follow the EYFS curriculum, which has seven main areas of learning.
Personal, Social, and Emotional Development Communication and Language Physical Development
Literacy Mathematics Understanding the World Expressive Arts
Our children encounter reading, writing, and numeracy through a variety of adult-led and child-initiated activities. We encourage their enthusiasms, supplying enjoyable and appropriately challenging opportunities for them to develop and become more resilient and independent. Accurate observation informs our planning for each child, ensuring that learning is consistent and that all children make the best possible progress. Knowing our families and children well, and working closely with them, we offer varied, stimulating means of progressing children’s knowledge and understanding of themselves, our local community, and beyond. Children move up to the Junior School confident and eager to learn. Our integrated structure smoothes the transition and ensures that children’s interests, needs, and progress remain a focus.
We encourage our children to question, investigate, and explore. Our extensive outdoor facilities, designated outside learning area, forest school, and pond activities inspire and develop our children’s imagination and creativity. Part of a larger school community, our children enjoy excellent specialist sport and music facilities, more opportunities to discover the world around them, and interactions with children of different ages. Co-curricular activities and educational visits further enhance our pupils’ discovery of new and diverse experiences, developing the key characteristics of playing and learning.

Senior School
Welcome to the Senior School
We offer our senior pupils a vibrant and stimulating learning environment with bright, airy classrooms, cutting edge facilities, and extensive grounds. Our broad, inclusive curriculum allows pupils to follow their individual interests, and inspiring teaching, delivered by enthusiastic and dedicated subject specialists, engages our pupils, instilling in them the skills necessary for success and a love of learning.
Our small class sizes mean our pupils receive a personalised education, carefully tailored to an individual’s needs. Ambitious for our children, we regularly review their progress so that they continue to be appropriately challenged and nurtured. We strive for everyone to exceed their potential, ensuring that our gifted and talented pupils are stimulated and pupils with SEND supported.
Focused on holistic care, with our children’s well-being at the heart of what we do, we work in close partnership with parents and pupils to ensure that our pupils make excellent progress towards their personalised targets and the ultimate goal of achieving GCSEs that reflect their ability and potential.
As an inclusive school, adding value is an important focus, and we achieve impressive successes. Many pupils achieve well above their standardised predictions, and some gain more than two grades above these in a range of subjects. We believe that a number of factors drives this success: excellent teaching, high contact time with pupils in small classes, a supportive ethos, and a culture that fosters ambition and learning.
Our caring community develops compassionate, thoughtful individuals with growth mindsets, and we invest in enabling our children to expand and enhance their soft skills and social conscience. Our pupils benefit from a diverse range of exciting opportunities that promote leadership, strong communication, problem solving, and collaboration. We work closely with Brighton Homeless and Vulnerable Charity – Off the Fence, and we have gold accreditation for our involvement in the Youth Parliament Democracy Awards. Our pupils are role models for our younger children, and play a key role, as part of our lively community, in supporting their development and well-being. We cultivate enthusiasm, confidence, and resilience in our children, and equip them with the skills they will need during their time at Shoreham College and beyond.

About Us
Welcome to Shoreham College
Shoreham College offers all the advantages of an all-through integrated education. Children learn together and thrive in our welcoming community. We choose to be co-educational, teaching girls and boys together from the ages of 3 to 16, knowing that this better prepares our pupils for a world in which the sexes live and work alongside each other.
We recognise that every child has their own strengths and challenges, and we believe that by learning together in an inclusive and kind environment, our pupils learn to respect and value one another, irrespective of gender and other differences.
Shoreham College pupils benefit from excellent facilities, caring support staff, and specialist teachers. From a young age, our junior pupils gain from specialist senior resources as well as from regular interaction and friendship with older pupils. In turn, our senior pupils become leaders and role models to our youngest children. Our learning community enables each member to grow and flourish.
We offer a broad and balanced curriculum, designed to develop a range of transferable skills and talents and to appeal to every interest. As they progress through the school, our children benefit from the continuity our integration provides and from being a valued individual within our community. Our knowledge of our pupils’ needs and passions means these remain a focus, and as our attainment data shows, our children are protected from the attainment dip that too often characterises the move from KS2 to KS3. Smooth transition between year groups and key stages ensures pupils maintain and build on their progress without interruption.

Aims and Ethos
Aims and Ethos
Shoreham College is a leading independent day school for girls and boys aged 3 to 16.
We are a mainstream school committed to providing a stimulating, vibrant education to children across a range of abilities, and to ensuring all our pupils achieve their full potential. We strive to:
At the heart of our local community, Shoreham College is a family school in every sense. We value every individual in our community for who they are. Understanding that happiness and well-being are essential for achievement and progress, we are ambitious for our pupils within a nurturing community. Our compassionate ethos is at the centre of everything we do.
Our pupils benefit from an extensive curriculum and superb facilities and teaching. Small class sizes ensure every child enjoys an education tailored to their needs and an appropriate level of challenge and support. A genuinely mixed ability school, we are experienced in providing an excellent, personalised education.
Playing an active role in our community is important to us. Our children learn to be good citizens whilst developing crucial social and leadership skills. We work with Brighton Homeless and Vulnerable Charity – Off the Fence, and have gold accreditation from the Youth Parliament Democracy Awards. In school, we foster a friendly, kind environment with our children’s well-being paramount. We are a beacon school for mindfulness, and await formal accreditation for our work on diversity. Our thriving forest school allows our pupils to explore and appreciate the natural world.
In choosing Shoreham College for your child, you place in us a huge amount of trust and responsibility. The best way to understand what makes Shoreham College special is to visit us. Our principal, Mrs Sarah Bakhtiari, will be delighted to show you around and to introduce you to our wonderful community. We extend the warmest of welcomes to you and your family at any time of the school year.
